subject: Hosted evaluation: mini-pilot actions & rate-slicing
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@minicart.com>, Priya Sinha <psinha@minicart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation: mini-pilot actions & rate-slicing

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap + suggested next actions to get a hosted evaluation (mini-pilot) moving:  

What we heard from the call
- Minicart wants fast, commerce-safe completions for product search & cart assist. Expected peak: ~120 qps at peak hour, average ~25 qps.
- Concern: payment/PII handling and latency SLAs (~ <250ms 95th for small completions).
- Team: 2 backend engineers + 1 infra (for preflight); timeline: 2–4 week pilot.

Why Hosted as a first step
- Fastest to get running for edge UX tests and traffic-shaped experiments; no infra lift for your team.
- We can give a sandbox endpoint, test keys, and a scoped rate window to mirror your peak traffic.
- If you need stricter PCI scoping later, we can evolve to Dedicated or Private VPC (we'll outline that below).

Proposed mini-pilot plan (hosted mode) — 3 bullets then actions
1) Quickstart sandbox (1–2 days): we provide a sandbox endpoint + test API key. Default throttle: 50 rps baseline, 200 rps burst for short tests. Token window: 4k tokens per request for the trial.
2) Integration preflight (1 week): your backend engineers run 1000s of synthetic flows against the sandbox; we validate latency, prefix cache benefits, and KV/session behavior.
3) Pilot run (2–4 weeks): gradually ramp traffic to a production-like slice (we recommend starting at 10% of your expected peak QPS, then 50%, then full). We’ll enable prefix/KV caching suggestions to reduce unit cost.

Immediate asks from your side
- Confirm expected sustained QPS during the pilot (you mentioned ~25 qps avg / 120 qps peak — can you confirm).
- Any strict data residency or retention constraints (EU, APAC, PCI requirements)?
- Who are the two engineers to invite to the preflight call?

Next steps from our side
- I’ll share: sandbox endpoint, a short quickstart doc, and a temporary test API key (attached). Marissa (cc'd) will follow up on commercial terms and pilot credits. Ben will standby for any infra/ops questions.

Attachments: Hosted-Eval-Quickstart.pdf (quick checklist + sample curl), mini-pilot-scope.xlsx (scope + nominal traffic buckets)

If that plan sounds good, can we lock a 30-minute preflight on Thursday 9/21 or Friday 9/22?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Chloe — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates:  

1) PCI / payment handling: our checkout flow touches card tokens. Does the hosted sandbox (and hosted production) avoid card data egress to Redwood entirely if we tokenise client-side? If not, is Private VPC the recommended path?

2) Latency SLA: you mentioned <250ms 95th — is that an SLA for hosted customers or an engineering target? We need to understand typical 95th P95 numbers for 512-token completions in us-west.

3) Rate shaping: curious about your recommendation for steady-state vs burst behaviour; our traffic has short spikes (10s) during flash discounts. Can the hosted path absorb 200 rps bursts for a few minutes without throttling, or should we plan for autoscale / fallback to a cheaper model?

Also — when you say "temporary test API key" — is that a single key we can share across devs or per-engineer keys?

If you can answer the above I can confirm the engineers and the Thursday/Friday slots.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: mini-pilot actions & rate-slicing

Samir — good questions. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) PCI / payment handling
- Short answer: hosted endpoints do not ingest raw card PANs if you tokenize client-side; you should avoid sending card numbers to any inference endpoint. For use cases where Redwood would touch card data (rare), Private VPC / on-prem is the recommended path and we have enterprise add-ons for PCI scope. For your plan (tokenize client-side + only send product/context to the model), hosted is appropriate for the mini-pilot.

2) Latency: SLA vs empirical numbers
- Hosted SLA: for our paid Hosted customers we offer a latency SLO (example: 95th <= 300ms for <= 128-token completions under normal load tiers). SLA with credits is part of Dedicated/Enterprise offers.
- Empirical (us-west, normal cache-hit rate): median ~60–90ms, P95 ~160–250ms for 512-token-ish completions on the models we demoed. We will run the same tests in your sandbox to produce a P95 baseline you can attach to acceptance criteria.

3) Rate shaping & bursts
- Hosted is built to absorb short bursts via warm pools and burst capacity, but sustained high burst minutes should be routed to autoscale/Priced Dedicated burst or a cheaper model fallback. For your use case we recommend: baseline throttle = 50 rps, burst to 200 rps (minutes-long) — that should be fine for flash discounts, but we will monitor and recommend a canary fallback model if needed.

4) API keys and sandbox access
- We’ll give you per-engineer API keys if you want (recommended). The initial artifact attached is a scoped test key bundle (sandbox-credentials.txt) with one global key and instructions to request per-user keys via our console.

Attachments included: sandbox-credentials.txt (API key + short curl examples)

Commercial / pilot credits
- Marissa (cc'd) will propose a 6K credit package for the mini-pilot and a short term pricing sheet for Hosted throughput during the pilot.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
- Confirm engineers (names/emails) for preflight.
- Book 30-min preflight: I have Thu 9/21 10:00–10:30 PDT or Fri 9/22 11:00–11:30 PDT. Which works?
- We'll enable sandbox endpoint: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/minicart and share per-engineer keys if you want them.

If that all looks right I’ll have Marissa follow with the commercial email with credits and a short pilot agreement. Ben is on standby to help with the preflight script and KV/prefix caching notes.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Chloe
